title: Without end
hook: God as the Infinite, beyond any description

segments.voice: Yesterday, Sefer Yetzirah, where letters are engraved, weighed and combined to form the world. Your line: letters create. Today, a name that refuses every line.

How do you draw something with no edges? Every drawing starts with a line, and a line is a boundary: this is inside, that is outside. A word works the same way. Call something kind, and you've drawn a line around it, kind and not cruel. Now try it with God. Every word you reach for draws a line. Wise. Strong. Near. Each one is true in its way, and each one is too small. Jewish mystics gave that problem a name, a name that is really a refusal to draw any line at all.
screen: `EVERY DRAWING STARTS WITH A LINE.` → `EVERY WORD DRAWS A BOUNDARY.` → `EACH ONE IS TOO SMALL.`

segments.voice: Ein Sof. In Hebrew, ein means there is no, and sof means end. Without end. Kabbalists use it for God as God is in God's own self, before and beyond any way of being known. First, it's hardly a name. A name usually tells you what something is. This one tells you only what it is not: not ending, not bounded, not measured. After weeks with Maimonides, you'll hear a cousin of his teaching, that we speak more truly of God by saying what God is not. The kabbalists take that silence and give it a title. Second, the Psalms point the same way. The psalmist praises God, then admits that God's greatness is beyond searching out. Praise, and then the edge of what praise can do. Third, Ein Sof is not a second God hiding behind the first. Kabbalists insist that God is one. Ein Sof is the one God from the side that can't be spoken of: not a different being, but the same One, seen from where every word runs out. Fourth, the turn. If God is without end, beyond every description, how does God touch a world with edges, a world of kitchens and buses and birthdays? That question drives the whole system ahead, and the mystics answer it with lights. For today, just stand where they stood, at the edge of the drawing, looking at the space with no line around it.
screen: `THERE IS NO END.` · `A NAME THAT SAYS WHAT GOD IS NOT.` · `NOT A SECOND GOD.` · `HOW DOES THE ENDLESS TOUCH THE WORLD?` · then, large: `WITHOUT END.`

segments.voice: Go to a window or step outside if you can, or close your eyes and remember the widest sky you've ever seen, and let your eyes rise past the roofs and wires and trees to where there's nothing to rest on. When your gaze wants an edge, a cloud, a bird, let it keep going instead. If you pray, you can simply be quiet before the One without end.
Ein Sof. Without end: the kabbalists' way of speaking of God as God is in God's self, beyond every name and description. Today's word.
Your line: without end. Every word for God draws a line; this name refuses to. Day one thousand one hundred seventy-four, done.

howItsDone: In Kabbalah, Ein Sof is the term for God beyond all description; students usually meet it at the start of an introduction to the sefirot, as the one source from which everything else unfolds.

chat.says: Is Ein Sof a different God from the God of the Bible?
options: No. Kabbalists insist God is one; Ein Sof is the same One, beyond every word.
Yes. It's a hidden God standing behind the God who speaks in the Torah.
No, it's a name for the angels who carry God's throne in Ezekiel's vision.
